title: Route telemetry for embeddings & rerank: cost-trace correlation and adaptive SLO alerting
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: produce a single route-focused telemetry surface that ties together per-request cost attribution, causal tracing for the embeddings + rerank pipeline, and adaptive SLO alerts. Currently teams can see aggregate embedding usage and siloed traces, but it is hard to answer: which user-facing route is incurring the largest rerank cost, which stage causes 99th percentile latency, and whether a cost spike is driven by model variant, sequence length, or workload shift.

This ticket will: (1) add structured span tags to traces emitted by the rerank pipeline (candidate_fetch, embed_lookup, vector_score, rerank_forward, post_process); (2) emit per-request billing tags (model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, quant_profile, routing_tier) to metrics and traces; (3) add a cost-attribution transform in the metrics pipeline to assign GPU-time and token cost back to route keys; (4) build a Grafana/Console route dashboard with waterfall cost breakdown, span-duration heatmap, 95/99 latency trend, and chargeback per 1000 requests; (5) implement adaptive alerting ("SLOPulse") that combines absolute thresholds with rolling-baseline anomaly detection to reduce alert noise during planned traffic shifts.

Why unique: previous work focused on per-route visibility for embed-rerank but left cost allocation and causal trace correlation underdeveloped. This ticket emphasizes a joined view (trace + cost + route) and an alerting model that adapts to seasonality to reduce pager fatigue for SREs and product owners.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing: all rerank request paths include the required span names and tags (candidate_fetch, embed_lookup, vector_score, rerank_forward, post_process) and include route_key and model_variant metadata.
Cost attribution: per-request cost estimate (tokens, GPU-ms, net token-cost) is computed and available as a labeled metric with route_key and model_variant tags in production metrics store.

Dashboards: Route-level dashboard template exists in Console/Grafana showing cost waterfall, span-duration heatmap, P50/P95/P99 latency, requests per second, and cost per 1k requests. Template is linked and accessible to PMs/Engineering.
Alerting: SLOPulse rules are deployed to staging; they trigger for synthetic traffic anomalies and respect maintenance windows. Documentation for alert thresholds and escalation is published.
Regression: unit/integration tests cover tagging and cost transform logic; load tests show <5% overhead on request path for added instrumentation.
Rollout: gradual rollout plan executed (canary on internal routes -> 10% customer routes -> all) with rollback steps documented.
tasks: Add structured span instrumentation to the rerank codepath (C++ runtime + Python request proxy) - include route_key and model_variant tags.
Emit token counts and quant_profile to trace/span attributes at ingress and post-generation.
Implement a cost-attribution lambda in metrics pipeline (compute GPU-ms * model_cost + token-cost) and label by route_key.
Create Grafana panels and Console dashboard template that accept route_key as a variable and show cost/time waterfall and span heatmap.
Prototype SLOPulse: combine absolute threshold rules with rolling-median anomaly detector (7d window) and add silencing for planned spikes.
End-to-end tests: synthetic replay to validate attribution correctness and alert triggers; measure instrumentation overhead under load.
Document runbook: how to interpret route breakdown, how to remediate common causes (model variant regressions, long tail due to candidate explosion), and rollback steps.
Ship PRs for telemetry, metrics transform, dashboard JSON, and alert rules; get design/PM approvals before canary.
Post-deploy: collect feedback from two product teams and iterate on thresholds and dashboard layout.
Close with a short postmortem/lessons-learned note and suggested next steps (per-tenant cost allocation, per-customer quota alerts).
